_doc: Registry of factual claims used in the library, each paired with a public source.
Every numeric or specific factual claim in an article should either:
(a) appear here with a source URL, or
(b) be labeled illustrative/directional in the prose itself, or
(c) be sourced inline via a <details class="cite">…</details> drawer.
If a claim doesn't fit one of those three patterns, it doesn't belong in the library.
When in doubt, cut. When the source is private (operator experience), label it as such.
claim:       the factual assertion as written
source_url:  primary public URL (vendor pricing page, search-industry analysis, Google docs, etc.)
date_verified: YYYY-MM-DD when last checked against the source
used_in:     list of article slugs (or page paths) that cite this claim
notes:       what to watch for if the source changes

ai_overview_share_march_2025.claim: Google AI Overviews appeared on 13.14% of US desktop queries in March 2025
ai_overview_share_march_2025.notes: The 13.14% figure was reported by Search Engine Land in a March 2025 analysis. The library cites the publication and the article's date-and-title in the citation drawer with a link to the publication's home page rather than a deep article URL — Search Engine Land restructures article slugs periodically, and a stale deep link reads worse than letting the reader find the piece via search. Post-March-2025 trajectory is reported qualitatively.

doordash_marketplace_tiers.claim: DoorDash Marketplace commission tiers: Basic 15%, Plus 25%, Premier 30%
doordash_marketplace_tiers.notes: Re-check quarterly. DoorDash renames tiers and reorganizes their merchant-help URL structure periodically; the percentage-bands have held since 2022. The library links to the DoorDash merchant docs home page rather than a specific learning-center slug, so the link doesn't break when DoorDash reorganizes.

google_local_ranking_signals.claim: Google ranks local results by distance, relevance, and prominence — and review-response activity is one of the signals weighted toward prominence
google_local_ranking_signals.source_name: Google Business Profile Help — Improve your local ranking
google_local_ranking_signals.notes: Google support answer IDs are stable; this URL has been live and unchanged for several years. Kept as deep-link.

google_business_profile_help_photos.claim: Google states that businesses with photos receive significantly more directions requests and click-throughs than businesses without
google_business_profile_help_photos.source_name: Google Business Profile Help — Add photos and videos
google_business_profile_help_photos.notes: Google has cited specific percentages (42% more directions, 35% more click-throughs) in their documentation. The exact numbers shift over time; the directional finding is consistent.

dc_initiative_82.claim: DC Initiative 82 phases out the tipped minimum wage in the District of Columbia
dc_initiative_82.notes: Government-agency sites occasionally restructure their policy pages. The library links to the agency home page so the citation doesn't rot the next time DOES reorganizes; the policy is searchable by name (Initiative 82 / Tipped Wage Workers Fairness Amendment Act) from the DOES home.

instagram_2024_algorithm_update.claim: Meta's late-2024 algorithm update penalizes stacked-hashtag posts
instagram_2024_algorithm_update.notes: Meta's official wording on the change is in creator-blog announcements; specific percent-penalty figures are not published. Treat the directional effect as cited, the magnitude as qualitative. The library links to the creator hub home page since Meta moves blog-post URLs around as the site reorganizes.

nielsen_norman_group_reference.claim: Nielsen Norman Group has published research on local-business website usability and on Fitts's Law
nielsen_norman_group_reference.notes: Two specific NNG article URLs previously cited in the library (`/articles/local-business/` and `/articles/fittss-law/`) returned 404s — they were never the canonical NNG slugs for the research they referenced. The library now credits Nielsen Norman Group by name with a link to the home page; readers can search nngroup.com for the specific piece. The substantive claims (local-business website usability research; Fitts's Law) are well-documented research topics NNG covers, so the source attribution stands. Any future NNG citation must paste the live URL from a browser visit before publishing.

baymard_institute_reference.claim: Baymard Institute has published research on cart-abandonment rates in e-commerce
baymard_institute_reference.notes: The previously cited URL path (`/lists/cart-abandonment-rate`) is not the canonical slug under which Baymard publishes its cart-abandonment meta-analysis. The library now credits Baymard Institute by name with a link to the home page; the cart-abandonment list is reachable from the Baymard navigation. Any future Baymard citation must paste the live URL from a browser visit before publishing.

think_with_google_mobile_speed.claim: Think with Google has published research on mobile page-speed industry benchmarks
think_with_google_mobile_speed.notes: Think with Google reorganizes its content sections periodically. The library now credits Think with Google by name with a link to the home page; the page-speed benchmarks piece is searchable from there. Any future Think-with-Google citation must paste the live URL from a browser visit before publishing.

_doc: Claims that come from Don's restaurant-floor experience rather than a public source.
These ARE allowed in articles, but must be framed as operator practice — not as measured data.
If a claim says 'in operator practice' / 'we typically see' / 'restaurants we audit' it goes here.
If a claim says '42% of our diagnostics' / '600 reviews across two restaurants' it does NOT — it's pretending to be measurement and must come out.
